patches.replacement_text: The literal stem asks whether "you" were approached by community and/or political party representatives; the question text does not identify who "you" is, so the addressee (interviewer or other administration-side reporter) is unresolved and must not be inferred. The field records only whether such an approach occurred, not who approached or what was said.

The physical-threat item is separately worded from the felt-threat item; the packet gives only these distinct stems and the co-occurrence of the two reports within any interview is unobserved, so no nesting, implication, or directional relation is asserted.
Separate interviewer-side item worded around physical threats specifically, distinct in wording from the felt-threat stem; co-occurrence is unobserved.

Single-choice attribution of which actor should ensure elected legislators do their jobs, drawn from the fixed actor list: 0 = The President / Executive, 1 = The Parliament / local government council, 2 = Their Political Party, 3 = The Voters, 4 = No One, with special codes -1 = Missing, 8 = Refused, 9 = Don't know, 93 = Not asked in Burkina Faso after 4th of October, 94 = Not asked in country.

A single actor nomination from a fixed list assigning who should ensure elected MPs do their jobs, with options 0 = The President / Executive, 1 = The Parliament / local government council, 2 = Their Political Party, 3 = The Voters, 4 = No One, and special codes -1 = Missing, 8 = Refused, 9 = Don't know, 93 = Not asked in Burkina Faso after 4th of October, 94 = Not asked in country.

The two attribution items are separately worded: Q48A asks who should ensure that, once elected, [members of Parliament] do their jobs, and Q48B asks who should ensure that, once elected, the [president] does [his] job. The packet supports only these separate stems and does not support a shared-actor inference, so the two are described as distinct items and are not merged.
